s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive eruption of papules and nodules over a 2-year period in a child
salient_findings: Multiple yellow to reddish brown firm papules and nodules on the scalp, face, neck, trunk, and limbs
Lesions coalescing into yellow-brown nodules and plaques up to 4 cm in diameter
Involvement of nasal and oropharyngeal mucosa
key_facts: 7-year-old boy presented with a 2-year history of progressive eruption of papules and nodules
Lesions did not cause pain or itching
No family history of cutaneous disorders
Lesions were 2 to 10 mm in diameter
Routine laboratory test results and serum chemistry with serum lipid levels were within normal ranges
No clinical evidence of internal involvement was found on ultrasonography, computed tomography, or magnetic resonance imaging results
Dense diffuse cellular infiltrate composed mainly of foamy histiocytic cells and multinucleated Touton cells mixed with lymphocytes and eosinophils
Positive for CD68 and CD163, but negative for S100, CD1a, and Langerin on immunohistochemical staining

shortlist.label: Juvenile xanthogranuloma
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation of progressive eruption of papules and nodules, histopathological findings of foamy histiocytic cells and Touton cells, and immunohistochemical staining positive for CD68 and CD163

shortlist.label: Non-Langerhans cell histiocytosis
shortlist.why_kept: Histopathological findings of dense diffuse cellular infiltrate composed mainly of foamy histiocytic cells and multinucleated Touton cells, and lack of family history of cutaneous disorders

shortlist.label: Xanthoma disseminatum
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation of disseminated, yellowish, xanthomatous maculopapular lesions and nodules, and histopathological findings of foamy histiocytic cells and Touton cells

shortlist.label: Generalized eruptive histiocytoma
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation of progressive eruption of papules and nodules, and histopathological findings of dense diffuse cellular infiltrate composed mainly of foamy histiocytic cells

shortlist.label: Benign cephalic histiocytosis
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation of progressive eruption of papules and nodules, and histopathological findings of foamy histiocytic cells and Touton cells, although less likely due to the age of the patient and the extent of the lesions

raw.rationale: The presence of foamy histiocytic cells and multinucleated Touton cells, along with the clinical presentation of yellowish, xanthomatous maculopapular lesions and nodules, is consistent with juvenile xanthogranuloma. The immunohistochemical staining profile, including positivity for CD68 and CD163, also supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Non-Langerhans cell histiocytosis
rejected.why: While the histiocytic infiltrate is consistent with this diagnosis, the specific presence of Touton cells and the clinical presentation are more characteristic of juvenile xanthogranuloma.

rejected.label: Xanthoma disseminatum
rejected.why: This condition typically presents with a more widespread and symmetric distribution of lesions, and the histopathological findings do not exactly match those described in the vignette.

rejected.label: Generalized eruptive histiocytoma
rejected.why: The clinical presentation and histopathological findings do not align with this diagnosis, which typically presents with a more acute onset and a different immunohistochemical staining profile.

rejected.label: Benign cephalic histiocytosis
rejected.why: This condition is typically limited to the head and neck region, and the histopathological findings do not match those described in the vignette.
